- Current tracked lines remain 34,047 total with diff -4,028 versus baseline, so another large reduction slice is required.
- I am evaluating unfinished config/test-boundary plans and the corresponding code paths to pick the next highest-yield seam instead of blindly reusing the last completed plan.
- Next I will settle on a specific reduction target and write the next plan file plus task pointer update, then stop as instructed for planning mode.

- Verified the current config/test rendering owner: load_config.rs still owns string-overlay merging and exposes toml_* helpers consumed mainly by HA fixture code.
- I am now checking exact remaining callers and file sizes so the new plan names a deletion boundary that is both high-yield and realistically executable next turn.
- After that I will write the next plan file, repoint the task to it, and stop immediately.

- The stale delete-public-renderers plan is close to the live code but not accurate enough: the public cfg-gated re-export corridor still exists today in config_v2/mod.rs and parser/mod.rs.
- I am checking whether removing external callers would also let the runtime/operator TOML renderer helpers become private or disappear, which is the real line-reduction lever.
- Next I will write a fresh current-state-aware plan file and repoint the task to it.

- Chose the next reduction slice and wrote .ralph/tasks/story-config-v2-direct-cfg-collapse/05-reduce-loop_plans/93-localize-config-test-string-support-and-delete-export-corridor.md.
- Repointed 05-reduce-loop.md to the new plan and marked the plan tail as NOW EXECUTE so the next turn should execute that slice instead of replanning.
- Verified the design target: delete the config_v2 public string-helper export corridor by moving HA/observer/CLI fixture rendering back to their owning tests while keeping parser-only helpers private.

- Read prior codex progress and confirmed the active Ralph task pointer is .ralph/tasks/story-config-v2-direct-cfg-collapse/05-reduce-loop.md.
- I am reading the task body and the relevant reduction skill to determine whether this turn is execution against the prepared plan or a design-verification stop.
- Next I will inspect the linked plan marker and then either execute the slice or switch it back to TO BE VERIFIED if the design boundary no longer fits the current code.

- Loaded the reduce-loop task body and confirmed it explicitly points at plan 93 for this turn.
- I am now reading the plan and the current call graph around config TOML/string helper functions to check whether the prepared execution slice still matches live code.
- Next I will decide whether plan 93 remains executable as-is; if yes I will implement it, otherwise I will switch the marker back to TO BE VERIFIED and stop.

- Plan 93 is marked NOW EXECUTE, so this turn should implement unless live code disproves the boundary.
- I am reading the helper definitions and import/export sites for the config TOML test-support corridor to map the exact edits before touching files.
- Next I will inspect the external callers and then patch the code to localize the remaining string/render helpers.

- Confirmed the export corridor still exists in config_v2/mod.rs and parser/mod.rs and the parser-side helpers are still defined in load_config.rs.
- I am reading the three external consumers and the parser test module to finalize which helpers should move local versus stay private inside the parser owner.
- Next I will patch those callers and then remove the now-dead re-exports and helper functions.

- The main remaining design question is whether HA givens can own their runtime fixture text without copying too much baseline TOML.
- I am checking whether the public config types already support serialization or another caller-owned render path that would keep the slice code-reducing instead of duplicative.
- Next I will either proceed with the local renderers or, if that boundary duplicates too much, switch the plan back to TO BE VERIFIED and stop.

- The public config types are not a useful caller-owned serialization path because RuntimeConfigV2 itself is not serializable.
- I am checking private-schema defaults now to see whether the old shared runtime renderer was overproducing TOML and can be replaced with much smaller caller-local minimal documents.
- Next I will either implement those smaller local renderers or, if the runtime baseline is too large to duplicate responsibly, switch the plan back to TO BE VERIFIED.

- The private schema confirms that cluster/postgres/dcs are the real required runtime sections and many old defaults can be omitted from caller-owned fixture TOML.
- I am checking process/logging defaults now so the new local renderers stay minimal while still passing loader validation.
- Next I will patch the three external callers and then delete the export corridor and parser-only helper surface.

- Patched the three external callers to own their config fixture rendering and removed the public re-export corridor from config_v2/mod.rs and parser/mod.rs.
- I am doing a quick structural review of the edited code now to catch unused constants/imports and any obvious TOML-shape mistakes before running formatter and the full validation suite.
- Next I will make any small cleanup edits, then run cargo fmt, line-count checks, and the required make targets.

- Applied the execution patch and formatted the code with cargo fmt.
- I am checking the tracked line counts and diff summary now to verify this slice actually reduced code before running the full validation suite.
- Next I will proceed with make check/lint/test/test-long if the line count moved in the right direction; otherwise I will reassess the slice.

- The slice failed the reduction gate: tracked lines rose to 34144 and the diff regressed to -3931, so I am not running the full make targets yet.
- I am searching for additional deletions inside the same config-render boundary, especially shared parser helpers that can now be inlined or removed after the export corridor was cut.
- Next I will either cut enough lines to turn the slice net-negative or, if the design cannot be made reducing, switch back to TO BE VERIFIED and stop.

- Collapsed the remaining parser-owned generic render machinery into minimal string emitters and moved the operator test renderer into the parser test module.
- I am rechecking the tracked line counts now to see whether those deletions recovered the regression and made this slice net-reducing.
- Next I will run the required make targets only if the slice is back below the previous 34047-line mark.

- make check and make lint both passed after tightening the imports and clippy-driven cleanup.
- make test compiled successfully but the nextest run reported a failing test, so I am reading the generated nextest junit/log files to identify the exact regression before changing code again.
- Next I will fix the failing behavior, rerun make test, and only then move on to make test-long.

- Final validation for this slice passed: make check, make lint, make test, and make test-long all succeeded after localizing the config test renderers and collapsing parser test-support machinery.
- Final measured reduction for this slice is back below the previous baseline gate, so I am capturing git status/line counts and then running Ralph task switch plus commit/push for this validated improvement.
- Next turn should pick the next reduction plan because the overall reduce-loop task still remains below the 19k target and must keep passes=false.
